Men's Basketball All-Americans|2011]]) }} '''Bradley Daniel Wanamaker''' (born July 25, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played four seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]]. Wanamaker earned an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection in [[2016–17 EuroLeague|2017]]. ==High school career== Born in [[Philadelphia]], Wanamaker went to [[Roman Catholic High School]] in his hometown, where he played high school basketball. In 2007, he was named the [[Philadelphia Daily News]]' Player of the Year as a high school senior. ==College career== Wanamaker then went on to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], where he played with the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]], under [[head coach]] [[Jamie Dixon]]. In his four years at Pitt, Wanamaker scored 1,090 points. [[2011 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|As a senior]], he was named an honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-American]], by the [[Associated Press]].{{cite web | title = Brad Wanamaker Pittsburgh Panthers profile | work = [[Pittsburgh Panthers]] | url = http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/wanamaker_brad00.html | access-date = November 19, 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160305072422/http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/wanamaker_brad00.html | archive-date = March 5, 2016 | url-status = dead }} ==Professional career== ===Teramo (2011)=== After going [[undrafted]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]], Wanamaker split time in the 2011–12 season between two Italian clubs, the first of which was [[Teramo Basket|Banca Teramo Basket]] === Forli (2012) === Wanamaker played for [[Fulgor Libertas Forli]] in 2012. === Austin Toros (2012) === Wanamaker returned to the United States to join the [[Austin Toros]]. He joined the Toros just in time to help the team to an [[NBA Development League]] title in 2012.{{cite web | title = Brad Wanamaker Signs With French Team Limoges | work = [[SLAM Magazine]] | date = August 15, 2012 | url = http://www.slamonline.com/online/news-rumors/other-news/2012/08/brad-wanamaker-signs-with-french-team-limoges/ | access-date = November 19, 2013}} Wanamaker had workouts with many [[NBA]] teams but was never offered a contract. He also competed in the [[NBA Summer League]] several times. === Limoges (2012–2013) === For the 2012–13 season, Wanamaker moved to [[Limoges CSP|Limoges]] of [[French basketball league system|France's top league]], the [[LNB Pro A]], where he averaged 9.0 [[points per game|points]] and 3.4 [[rebounds per game]].{{cite web | title = French League profile | work = [[LNB Pro A]] | url = http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200006/Joueurs/A55218/Brad-Wanamaker?saison=2012 | access-date = November 19, 2013}} === Pistoia (2013–2014) === The following season, Wanamaker returned to Italy and signed with [[Pistoia Basket 2000|Giorgio Tesi Pistoia]] of [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{cite web | title = Brad Wanamaker (ex Limoges) signs at Tuscany Pistoia | work = [[Eurobasket.com]] | date = August 6, 2013| url = https://www.eurobasket.com/Italy/basketball.aspx?NewsID=327514 | access-date = November 19, 2013}} === Brose (2014–2016) === On July 2, 2014, Wanamaker signed with [[Brose Baskets]] of Germany's [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{cite web|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/138235|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140707030610/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/138235|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 7, 2014|title=Bamberg strenghtens [sic] roster with Duncan and Wanamaker|work=Welcome to Eurocup}} With Bamberg, he won the [[2014–15 Basketball Bundesliga|2014–15 Bundesliga]] and was also named [[Basketball Bundesliga Finals MVP|Finals MVP]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/164882/brad-wanamaker-named-beko-bbl-finals-mvp.html|title=Brad Wanamaker named Beko BBL Finals MVP|date=June 21, 2015|work=Sportando}} On June 23, 2015, Wanamaker re-signed with Bamberg for one more season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/165111/brose-bamberg-extends-with-brad-wanamaker-and-janis-strelniekis.html|title=Brose Bamberg extends with Brad Wanamaker and Janis Strelniekis|date=June 23, 2015|work=Sportando}} In the [[2015–16 Euroleague|2015–16 season]], Brose played in the [[EuroLeague]], and had a solid season, in which the team reached the Top 16. In the German BBL, Wanamaker was named the [[Basketball Bundesliga MVP|Most Valuable Player]],{{cite web|url=http://www.beko-bbl.de/de/n/news/2016/5-mai/award-wanamaker-und-first-team/|title=Beko BBL – Award Wanamaker und First Team|access-date=May 13, 2016|archive-date=June 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617101455/http://www.beko-bbl.de/de/n/news/2016/5-mai/award-wanamaker-und-first-team/|url-status=usurped}} after leading the Bamberg team to a second straight national domestic league championship.{{Cite web|url=http://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/n/news/2016/6-juni/weekly-news2/|title=Beko BBL – Weekly News2|website=www.easycredit-bbl.de|access-date=July 21, 2016}} === Darüşşafaka (2016–2017) === On June 23, 2016, Wanamaker signed a two-year contract with Turkish club [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka Doğuş]].{{cite news|title=Darüşşafaka Doğuş signes Brad Wanamaker|url=http://www.darussafakadogusbasketbol.com/news-details.aspx?id=64163|access-date=June 24, 2016|work=darussafakadogusbasketbol.com|date=June 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420122416/http://www.darussafakadogusbasketbol.com/news-details.aspx%3Fid%3D64163|archive-date=April 20, 2019|url-status=dead}} === Fenerbahçe (2017–2018) === On September 7, 2017, Wanamaker signed a one-year contract with the [[2017 EuroLeague Final Four|2017 EuroLeague champions]], [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Doğus]].{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce tabs All-EuroLeague guard Wanamaker|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/846o3puy3b3t4p86/fenerbahce-tabs-all-euroleague-guard-wanamaker|access-date=September 7, 2017|work=euroleague.net|date=September 7, 2017}} In the [[2017–18 EuroLeague]] season, Fenerbahçe made it to the [[2018 EuroLeague Final Four]], its fourth consecutive [[EuroLeague Final Four|Final Four]] appearance. Eventually, they lost 85–80 to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in the final game.{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is 2018 EuroLeague champion|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=260&seasoncode=E2017#!report|access-date=May 20, 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=May 20, 2018}} In 36 EuroLeague games, he averaged 11.3 points, 2.7 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game, while shooting 41% on his field goal attempts. === Boston Celtics (2018–2020) === On July 2, 2018, Wanamaker signed a one-year contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web |title=Celtics Sign Brad Wanamaker |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-brad-wanamaker |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 2, 2018 |date=July 2, 2018}} Wanamaker made his NBA debut on October 16, recording two points and one rebound in a blowout 105–87 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20181016/PHIBOS#/boxscore |title=Archived copy |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=October 17, 2018 |archive-date=October 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017054349/http://www.nba.com/games/20181016/PHIBOS#/boxscore |url-status=dead }} On July 17, 2019, the Boston Celtics announced that they had re-signed Wanamaker.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-re-sign-daniel-theis-brad-wanamaker|title=Celtics Re-Sign Daniel Theis, Brad Wanamaker|date=July 17, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 17, 2019}} Wanamaker finished the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]] as the leader in free throw percentage.{{cite web|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/pitt/2020/08/28/pitt-panthers-basketball-brad-wanamaker-boston-celtics-nba-playoffs-philadelphia-kemba-walker/stories/202008300033|title=How Pitt grad Brad Wanamaker became the NBA's top free-throw shooter and a key piece off the Celtics' bench|website=post-gazette.com|last=Meyer|first=Craig|date=August 28, 2020|access-date=November 7, 2025}} === Golden State Warriors (2020–2021) === On November 24, 2020, Wanamaker signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/brad-wanamaker-20201124|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Guard Brad Wanamaker|work=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2020}} as a free agent to play backup point guard behind [[Stephen Curry]]. In 39 games, Wanamaker averaged 16 minutes and 4.7 points a game.{{Cite web|title=Brad Wanamaker Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/wanambr01.html|access-date=2021-07-10|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}} === Charlotte Hornets (2021) === On March 25, 2021, Wanamaker was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-brad-wanamaker-and-protected-2022-second-round-pick-golden-state|title=Hornets Acquire Brad Wanamaker and Protected 2022 Second-Round Pick from Golden State|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021}} after being out of the Warriors rotation since the All Star break.{{Cite web|title=Warriors trade Wanamaker to Hornets for 2025 second-round pick|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/warriors-trade-brad-wanamaker-hornets-2025-second-round-pick|access-date=2021-07-10|website=RSN|language=en}} === Indiana Pacers (2021) === On October 6, 2021, Wanamaker signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Trade Edmond Sumner to Brooklyn; Sign Brad Wanamaker to Training Camp Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-trade-edmond-sumner-brooklyn-sign-brad-wanamaker-training-camp-deal|website=NBA.com|date=October 6, 2021|access-date=October 6, 2021}} On December 27, he was waived.{{Cite web|title=Pacers Waive Wanamaker, Sign Sykes|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-wanamaker-sign-sykes|url-status=live|access-date=December 28, 2021|website=Indiana Pacers|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227173544/https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-wanamaker-sign-sykes |archive-date=December 27, 2021 }} === Washington Wizards (2021–2022) === On December 29, 2021, Wanamaker signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]] via the hardship exemption.{{cite news |last1=Todd |first1=Bijan |title=Report: Wizards Sign Guard Brad Wanamaker to 10-Day Deal |url=https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/sports/nbcsports/report-wizards-sign-guard-brad-wanamaker-to-10-day-deal/2922324/ |access-date=December 30, 2021 |work=NBC Washington
